The Police Sub-Inspector of R.T. Nagar Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code.
2. Prosecution Case:
The CW1 namely Smt. Shobha.H., married accused in the year 2003.

From the date of marriage, the accused under influence of alcohol ill treated CW1 by not providing basic necessities, failed to take care of his child and subjected CW1 to mental and physical cruelty and in the year 2016, the accused thrown the CW1 out from matrimonial house.

From then she resided with CW2 at No.39/1, 3rd Main, A.K.Ashrama, Meena Masjid, Matadahalli within the limits of R.T.
Nagara Police Station, Bengaluru with her son.

Even though, the accused did not take CW1 and her son back and went therein and picked up quarrel with CW1, abused, threatened her and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty thereby accused committed alleged offence.

3. First Information Report: On receipt of first information from CW1, CW5 namely Smt.
Premkumari, WPSI of R.T. Nagara Police Station registered Crime No.269/2020 against accused for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to her superior officers.

4. Investigation:
Thereafter she drawn spot mahazar on 05-11-2020, recorded the statement of witnesses, secured the photographs and documents and submitted charge sheet against accused for the alleged offence.
5. The accused was enlarged on bail by the order dated 12-04-2022.
6. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court has taken cognizance for the offence alleged against the accused.
7. Copies of prosecution paper as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned Senior APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence: The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 5 witnesses, examined 1 witness and exhibited 2 documents and closed their side.
During the cross examination of PW1, the counsel for accused has marked three documents as per Ex.D1 to D3.
On account of settlement arrived between PW1 and accused in MC No.1679/2021, the examination of remaining witnesses is dispensed with by the order dated 05/01/2026.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: After completion of evidence of prosecution, the accused was examined as per section 313 of Cr.P.C, wherein he denied all incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of prosecution witness and did not lead any rebuttal evidence.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the after marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Shobha with accused, the accused under influence of alcohol subjected CW1 to mental and physical cruelty and thrown her out of matrimonial house thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.498(A) of IPC?
2. What order?

13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1: In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined CW1 by name Smt Shailaja, being informant as PW1 who deposed that she got married to the accused on 13-06-2003 and after marriage, the accused under influence of alcohol ill-treated her, abused and beaten her,

15.
Evidence of Prosecution must be established that the accused persons subjected the PW1 to mental and physical cruelty.

Mere omnibus statement regarding harassment does not ipso facto makes out a case under section 498A IPC, prosecution is required to prove the overt acts attributed by the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt and the said principle is appreciated in case of Sakharam and another vs State of Maharastra reported in (2003) 12 SCC 368.

sentences.text:
Basing this decision,
the present cases are taken up for discussion.
16. It is relevant to reiterate Section 498A of Indian Penal Code which reads as under Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty --

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.

-- For the purposes of this section, "cruelty" means-- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

For commission of an offence under Section 498- A of IPC, the following necessary ingredients require to be satisfied:
(a) The woman must be married;
(b) She must be subjected to cruelty or harassment; and (c) Such cruelty or harassment must have been shown either by husband of the woman or by the relative of her husband and the said principle is appreciated in the case of U. Suvetha v. State reported in (2009) 6 SCC 757.
17.

entities.text: U. Suvetha v. State reported in (2009) 6 SCC 757
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Every harassment does not amount to "cruelty" within the meaning of Section 498-A.

For the purpose of Section 498-A, harassment simpliciter is not "cruelty" and it is only when harassment is committed for the purpose of coercing a woman or any other person related to her to meet an unlawful demand for property, etc. that it amounts to "cruelty" punishable under Section 498-A IPC Shobha H vs Prakash on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137199862/
4 and the said principle is appreciated in the case of State of A.P. vs. M. Madhusudhan Rao reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582.
18.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Cruelty can either be mental or physical.
It is difficult for straitjacket the term cruelty by means of a definition because cruelty is a relative term.

What constitutes cruelty for one person may not constitute cruelty for another person and the said principle is appreciated in the case of G.V.
Siddaramesh v. State of Karnataka reported in (2010) 3 SCC 152.

sentences.text: No doubt, this court cannot expect any evidence for the matrimonial offences when it was taken place within the four walls however the allegation made by the PW1 has to be proved by adducing cogent evidence.
Though the PW1 has initially supported the prosecution case however subsequent to the evidence given, deposed in her cross examination and re-examination as under Cross-examination of PW1

. 
   
   
   



      

 
 

   
 
 
 
 Re-examination by Sr
. APP:

Thus, it appears from the cross examination of PW1 being material witness did not support the prosecution case for coherence with the contents of complaint and chief-in-examination on account of settlement arrived in matrimonial case between the PW1 and the accused.
20.

This court is of the opinion that even if other witnesses were examined by the prosecution and they supported the prosecution case that would not helpful as PW1 herself did not support the prosecution case in the cross examination.

This court has dispensed with the examination of other witnesses which could be only formal in nature and hence taken the prosecution evidence as closed after examination of police official witnesses.

At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision in the case of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and another reported in (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only Shobha H vs Prakash on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137199862/
5 for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."

sentences.text: By basing aforesaid principle by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the above case is applicable to this case as well.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the Point No.1 is answered in the negative.
21. Point No.2-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.

(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C, his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
